subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, or keep `bootstrap-extra-files` limited to recognized workspace bootstrap filenames?
rationale: The code change is mechanically small, but it changes deterministic system-prompt context and file-loading scope for hook configuration, which is a product and security-boundary decision.

options.title: Approve guarded custom files
options.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or a replacement is rebased and preserves workspace guards, budgets, docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames only
options.body: Reject arbitrary workspace-file injection and close or redirect custom-file requests to narrower first-class filename or workspace-convention proposals.

options.title: Defer to broader context API
options.body: Pause this issue until maintainers choose a broader workspace discovery or context-file API instead of expanding the existing hook contract.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded custom files
recommendation.body: Allow explicitly configured custom-basename files through the existing hook path after the linked PR or a replacement is rebased and preserves workspace guards, budgets, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original hook feature and has recent ownership signals in the workspace bootstrap loader path.
